t: #3871 Count Commas in Range II — Digit-Length Buckets
o: A d-digit number carries floor((d-1)/3) commas. Group [1, n] by digit length: for each d, the count of d-digit numbers <= n times commas-per-number gives that bucket's contribution. n up to 1e15 means at most 16 buckets. Example: n = 1002 -> only the 4-digit bucket is partial (1000..1002, three numbers, one comma each) = 3; n = 998 -> 0.
k: Commas per number depend only on its digit count: floor((digits - 1) / 3).
Iterate digit lengths with powers of ten; clamp the top bucket at n.

a.i: Walk lo = 1, 10, 100, ...; each decade [lo, min(n, 10*lo - 1)] contains numbers of one digit length d; multiply its size by (d-1)//3.
s: While lo <= n: hi = min(n, lo*10 - 1).
Add (hi - lo + 1) * ((d-1) // 3) to ans; advance d and lo.
a.t: O(log10 n) — one iteration per digit length (at most 16).

w: Watch for overflow: (hi - lo + 1) * commas can exceed 32-bit ranges, so use 64-bit integers everywhere (JavaScript doubles handle 1e15 * 5 fine). Edge cases: n < 1000 returns 0; exact powers of ten. A follow-up might count a specific character like '1' across the range — that needs digit DP instead.
